.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 235 PM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Tonight through Tuesday:

Unseasonable warmth will continue to be the story for a few more
days, particularly on Monday. Tonight, given dew points this
afternoon in the mid to upper 50s in most spots, light 
southerly winds will enable overnight lows should to fall into 
the upper 50s to lower 60s (locally mid 50s) away from Chicago.
These readings are still 10-15F above average for the date,
providing a very mild starting point for Monday's warmth.

Some high cloud cover to start the day will give way to plenty
of sunshine through the afternoon. Forecast soundings support
southwesterly winds gusting up to 25 to 30 mph. With recent
dryness and 925 mb temps in the lower to mid 20s Celsius, the
setup looks prime for temps overperforming, reaching the mid to
upper 80s. Record highs for October 12th are relatively low
compared to surrounding days, making record highs a decent bet
at Chicago and Rockford (see climate section below). 

Can't completely rule out some high based sprinkles in spots on
Monday night in advance of an approaching cold front trailing 
from surface low pressure over northern Lake Michigan by early 
Tuesday. The cold front will otherwise move across the area 
with little fanfare on Tuesday. Exceptionally mild conditions
(60s to around 70F) to start Tuesday and very weak cold
advection will result in another day of summer-like temps,
though not quite as warm as those on Monday.

Tuesday Night through Sunday:

Anafrontal showers and some embedded thunderstorms are expected
at times later Tuesday evening into Wednesday morning. This will
occur as impulses riding fairly robust west-southwest mid-level
flow interact with moisture and modest elevated instability 
atop the baroclinic zone over the region. There's some
uncertainty with specifics in this period, including the
potential for axes of higher QPF. All in all, the fairly high 
PoPs in the official forecast appear warranted. High pressure
building down from the northern Great Lakes will shift showers
primarily south of I-80 by mid Wednesday morning. Any 
additional afternoon showers will probably be confined to mainly
south of the Illinois and Kankakee River Valleys (and perhaps
even primarily south of US-24). Highs on Wednesday, while still
above average for the date, will be noticeably cooler than
Tuesday, particularly along the lakefront (mid-upper 60s) due to
steady northeast winds.

The next period of interest for showers and embedded
thunderstorms is on Thursday. While there is considerable 
variance in the evolution of key synoptic features on Thursday,
including the track of weak surface low pressure, 60-70% PoPs
in the official forecast appear reasonable. A strong cold front
will sweep across the area Thursday night, with the coolest air
mass of the season thus far moving in behind the front for
Friday-Saturday. Seasonably strong (1030s to around 1040 mb)
high pressure transiting the region may set the stage for areas
of frost outside of Chicago Friday night into early Saturday and
Saturday night into early Sunday, depending on how cool surface 
temps actually get. Expect temps to quickly moderate back to 
near seasonable Sunday afternoon.

Castro

.AVIATION /00Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 618 PM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

VFR conditions will prevail through the TAF cycle. 

South-southwest winds will increase mid-late morning Monday,
likely gusting over 20kt late morning through the afternoon.
Gustiness of winds will ease toward sunset. West-southwest 
winds just off the surface will quickly increase to around 50kt
Monday evening. The strengthening winds just off the deck (at 
or below FL020) may result in surface winds to become gusty 
again Monday evening at ORD and MDW. If the surface gustiness 
doesn't materialize, then LLWS would be likely. Later TAFs 
updates will likely need to refine the forecast for MDW and ORD 
to either add gusts or LLWS.

- Izzi
